problem: The value $V(t)$ of a tech device varies according to the differential equation ${V}^{′}(t)=-rV(t),$ where $t$ is the time, measured in years, and $r>0.$ It is known that the value reduces by one-half after the first year. How long does it take for the value to reduce to one-fifth of its original value? Round your answer to one decimal place.

activity_context.topic_title: Exponential Growth and Decay Models With First-Order ODEs: Calculating Unknown Times and Initial Values

feedback.problem: The population $P(t)$ of mice in a forest varies according to the differential equation ${P}^{′}(t)=rP(t),$ where $t$ is the time, measured in months from the start of the observation period, and $r>0.$  It is known that the mouse population quintuples (increases fivefold) after the first two months. How long does it take for the mouse population to increase eightfold from the start of the observation period? Round your answer to one decimal place.
feedback.worked_solution:
The general solution to the given differential equation is

$$
P(t)={P}_{0}{e}^{rt},
$$

where ${P}_{0}$ is the mouse population when $t=0.$

Let ${t}_{1}$ be the time when the mouse population equals $8{P}_{0}.$ Then, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}P({t}_{1}) & =8{P}_{0}\,⇒\,{P}_{0}{e}^{r{t}_{1}}=8{P}_{0}.\end{aligned}
$$

We solve this equation for ${t}_{1},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{0}{e}^{r{t}_{1}} & =8{P}_{0} \\ \cancel{{P}_{0}}{e}^{r{t}_{1}} & =8\cancel{{P}_{0}} \\ {e}^{r{t}_{1}} & =8 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{r{t}_{1}}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ r{t}_{1} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡8 \\ {t}_{1} & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡8}{r}\,\,(∗)\end{aligned}
$$

We now need to calculate $r.$ We're told that the population quintuples after the first two months. Therefore,

$$
P(2)=5{P}_{0}\,⇒\,{P}_{0}{e}^{2r}=5{P}_{0}.
$$

We solve this equation for $r,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{0}{e}^{2r} & =5{P}_{0} \\ \cancel{{P}_{0}}{e}^{2r} & =5\cancel{{P}_{0}} \\ {e}^{2r} & =5 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2r}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ r & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this into $(∗)$ and evaluating, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}_{1} & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡8}{r} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡8}{(\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{2})} \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡8}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5} \\  & ≈2.6,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.
